How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to build and run a **RESTful GET** request for the *“get information of device connector versions”* API on **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll cover both the **web UI (API Explorer)** and a **command‑line / script** approach so you can pick whichever fits your workflow. --- ## 1. Using the Cisco Nexus Dashboard UI (API Explorer) | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **Login** | Open your browser → `https:///` → Enter credentials. | You need an authenticated session. | | **Navigate to API Explorer** | In the left‑hand menu, click **Developer** → **API Explorer**. | This is the built‑in tool for testing APIs. | | **Select API Version** | At the top of the page, there’s a drop‑down labeled **API Version**. Choose **6.3.1**. | Ensures you’re calling the correct schema. | | **Find the Endpoint** | Use the search box or the tree view to locate **Device Connector → Versions**. | The endpoint is usually `/api/v6.3.1/device-connector/versions`. | | **Configure the Request** | • Method: **GET**
• Path: `/api/v6.3.1/device-connector/versions`
• Query Params: (if any – e.g., `?limit=100`) | Set up the exact call you want to test. | | **Add Authentication** | The explorer automatically injects your session cookie or bearer token. If you’re using a custom header, click **Headers** → **Add Header** → `Authorization: Bearer `. | Required for protected endpoints. | | **Execute** | Click the **Execute** button. | Triggers the request. | | **Inspect Response** | The panel below shows status code, headers, and pretty‑printed JSON body. | Verify correctness and troubleshoot. | ### Quick Tips - **Save & Reuse**: After configuring, click **Save** → give it a name. You can load it later without re‑entering details. - **Export**: Click **Export** → choose **cURL** or **Python** to copy the request for scripts. - **History**: All executed calls appear in the **History** tab; useful for debugging. --- ## 2. Using cURL (Command Line) ```bash curl -X GET \ "https:///api/v6.3.1/device-connector/versions?limit=50" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -k # omit if you have a valid cert ``` - Replace `` with your actual host (e.g., `nexus.example.com`). - Replace `` with a JWT or OAuth token you obtained via the login flow. - Adjust query parameters (`limit`, `offset`, etc.) as needed. --- ## 3. Using Python (Requests Library) ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://" ENDPOINT = "/api/v6.3.1/device-connector/versions" TOKEN = "" headers = { "Accept": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}" } params = {"limit": 50} # optional response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}", headers=headers, params=params, verify=False) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` > **Note**: The `verify=False` flag disables SSL verification. Remove it in production. --- ## 4. Using the Provided Tool (`functions.requests_get`) If you prefer to let the system fetch the data directly, you can call the helper function: ```json { "url": "https:///api/v6.3.1/device-connector/versions?limit=50", "params": {} } ``` In practice, you’d replace the URL with the real one and optionally pass query parameters. The function will return the parsed JSON response. --- ## 5. Common Pitfalls & How to Fix Them | Issue | Symptom | Fix | |-------|---------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Status 401, empty body | Ensure the bearer token is fresh and has the right scopes. | | **404 Not Found** | Status 404 | Double‑check the path; maybe the endpoint changed in 6.3.1. | | **Rate‑Limit Exceeded** | Status 429 | Add `Retry-After` header handling or back‑off logic. | | **SSL Errors** | `ssl.SSLError` | Either use `-k`/`verify=False` or install the proper CA bundle. | --- ## 6. Next Steps 1. **Test** the endpoint in the UI first to confirm it works. 2. **Copy** the generated cURL or Python snippet for automation. 3. **Integrate** into your monitoring or provisioning scripts. 4. **Schedule** periodic checks if you need to keep the connector version list up‑to‑date. Happy querying!
